# @workerstack/ui

Fast, SSR-ready Solid 2 components on UI SDK, styled with Tailwind

## Contents

- [Usage](#usage)

## Usage

Styled Solid 2.0 components built on [UI SDK](https://ui-sdk.dev) (`@ui-sdk/solid`) and Tailwind CSS v4. UI SDK handles behavior and accessibility, and this package adds the styling.

### Install

```sh
bun add @workerstack/ui @ui-sdk/core@beta @ui-sdk/solid@beta cn solid-js@^2 @solidjs/web@^2 tailwindcss@^4
```

The package has no dependencies of its own. Everything it imports is a peer dependency, so your app owns one copy of each and picks its versions.

### CSS setup

In `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
import { ui } from "@workerstack/ui/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [solid(), tailwindcss(), ui()] });
```

In your app stylesheet:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "./ui.generated.css"; /* added by the plugin when missing */
```

The plugin writes `ui.generated.css` beside each CSS file that imports tailwindcss. It holds UI SDK's base styles, the theme from `ui.config.ts`, and the classes of exactly the exports your app imports and of the installed packages that use `@workerstack/ui`. If the CSS file lacks the second import, the plugin adds it after `@import "tailwindcss";`. The file is generated, so you can git-ignore it. `@tailwindcss/node` and `@tailwindcss/oxide` are peer dependencies. Installing `@tailwindcss/vite` brings both. The plugin needs `vite` 6.1 or later.

#### ui.config.ts

`ui.config.ts` at the Vite root is optional. Without it, dark mode uses `"class"` and no token is set.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@workerstack/ui/config";

export default defineConfig({
  dark: "class",
  tokens: { radius: "0.75rem", primary: { light: "oklch(0.55 0.2 255)", dark: "oklch(0.7 0.17 255)" } },
  colors: { brand: "oklch(0.7 0.15 30)" },
});
```

- `dark`: `"class"` (default) lets `.dark`, `.light` and `data-theme` force a scheme. `"media"` follows the system only.
- `tokens`: UI SDK's `--ui-*` tokens, by name without the prefix. Each is typed by its kind, so a length given to a color fails in the editor and in `tsc`. A color is a CSS color or `{ light, dark }`, which is written as `light-dark()`.
- `colors`: your own colors. `brand` becomes `--ui-brand` and a `bg-brand` utility. A token name is not allowed, and a name is lowercase like `brand` or `brand-muted`.

The plugin reruns when `ui.config.ts` or a file it imports changes. A bad config fails the build with a message that says what to fix.

Dark mode: put `class="dark"` or `data-theme="dark"` on a parent element (usually `<html>`). To re-theme, set `tokens` in `ui.config.ts`.

### Components

Every import path below is its own key in the package's export map, so a path that is not listed does not resolve. Each key is a folder, and `bun run sync:exports` writes the map from the folders.

| Import | Exports |
| --- | --- |
| `@workerstack/ui/utils/cn` | `cn` ([`cn`](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/cn)), `cnState` (merges state-function classes) |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/button` | `Button`, `buttonClass` (variants: primary, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive, link; sizes: sm, md, lg, icon) |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/field` | `Field`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError` |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/input` | `Input`, `InputGroup`, `InputClear` |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/select` | `Select`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel`, `SelectSeparator` |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/dialog` | `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger`, `DialogContent`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogClose` |
| `@workerstack/ui/components/menu` | `Menu`, `MenuTrigger`, `MenuContent`, `MenuItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `MenuRadioGroup`, `MenuRadioItem`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuGroupLabel`, `MenuSeparator`, `MenuShortcut`, `MenuSub`, `MenuSubTrigger`, `MenuSubContent` |

`class` on any part accepts a string, array, object, or a function of the part's state. It is merged with ours through tailwind-merge, so your classes win.

```tsx
import { Button } from "@workerstack/ui/components/button"
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldError } from "@workerstack/ui/components/field"
import { Input } from "@workerstack/ui/components/input"

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <Input type="email" />
  <FieldError>Required</FieldError>
</Field>
<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Save</Button>
```

Triggers (`DialogTrigger`, `MenuTrigger`, `DialogClose`) are unstyled. Give them `class={buttonClass({ variant: "outline" })}`.

### Translate the built-in strings

`UiProvider` takes `messages`, a `Partial<UiMessages>`: every key you leave out stays English, and a change re-renders in place.

```tsx
import { UiProvider } from "@workerstack/ui/components/provider"

<UiProvider messages={{ loading: "Učitavanje", close: "Zatvori", comboboxCreate: (label) => `Stvori „${label}”` }}>
  <App />
</UiProvider>
```

Each part keeps its English beside it, in a `<part>.messages.ts` file, so your bundle holds the English of the parts you import and no other. `UiMessages` lists every key the package translates.

### Development

From the repository root or from `packages/core`:

```sh
bun run typecheck
bun run test            # all three projects
bun run build           # emits dist/*.jsx + .d.ts, consumed via the "solid" export condition
```

#### Tests

Every component has four test files next to it:

| File | Project | Runs in | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `button.test.tsx` | `dom` | Chromium | The component's contract: roles, ARIA, state, events, class merging |
| `button.browser.test.tsx` | `browser` | Chromium with Tailwind and `base.css` | Real pointer and keyboard input, computed styles against the theme tokens, layout, focus |
| `button.server.test.tsx` | `server` | Node, Solid compiled for SSR | `renderToString` output: markup, ARIA, ids, classes, Solid warnings |
| `button.hydration.test.tsx` | `hydration` | HTML rendered in Node, hydrated in Chromium | The client claims every server node, with no hydration warnings, no replaced or added elements, and server ids kept; the hydrated component then works |

Components that tests render (fixtures) always live in the component's `__fixtures__/` folder, never inline in a test file: `src/components/dialog/__fixtures__/share-dialog.fixture.tsx` is shared by the dialog's tests, and `__fixtures__/dialog.hydration.fixture.tsx` is what both sides of the hydration test render. On the server it goes through the `serverRender` browser command that `solidHydration()` from `@workerstack/testing/web/solid/vitest` adds; in the browser it is compiled hydratable. Fixtures aren't published.

Run one with `bun run test:dom`, `test:browser`, `test:server` or `test:hydration`. Each project is its own `vitest.*.config.ts` with its own `solid()` plugin.

Helpers are in `src/test/`: `dom.ts` (`mounted`, `type`), `browser.ts` (`settled`, `token`, `style`, `rect`). The server, hydration, warning and pointer helpers come from `@workerstack/testing`: `/web/solid` (`renderServer`, `tag`, `tags`, `text`, `hydrator`, `recordWarnings`) and `/web/dom` (`pointer`).

A test marked `it.fails` pins a known UI SDK bug. Each one is written up, with its root cause and a fix idea, in [`docs/upstream/ui-sdk.md`](../docs/upstream/ui-sdk.md), ready for a PR. When an upgrade fixes one, its test starts failing: drop the `.fails` and mark the finding fixed.
